subject: Finability & payback path for Recommendation widget
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lim <sara@carelogix.com>, Marc Geller <marc.geller@carelogix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap + asks: Recommendation widget economics and next steps

Thanks again for taking time today — quick recap and concrete asks so we all have the same next steps. High-level: CareLogix is evaluating a personalized Recommendation widget you’ll surface in the patient portal; the key procurement questions are cost predictability, unit economics per feature, and time-to-payback for go-to-market spend.

Key points I captured from the call:
- Target launch: pilot Q4 2027 for 50k MAUs internal pilot, then phased rollout.
- Primary usage: 2–3 recommendation API calls per active user per day (mix of short prompts + model responses).
- Quality bar: high precision for clinical relevance — you indicated willingness to accept a slightly higher cost to avoid false positives.
- Procurement constraints: budget bandting is loose but procurement prefers <$150k/year for the pilot inference spend line item if possible.

Asks / data requests (please share by EOW):
1) Typical monthly token volume estimate for pilot (if you can provide DAU, avg queries/day, and avg tokens/query that helps us run scenarios).
2) Any internal target $/feature or budget cap for incremental features (this helps frame payback).
3) Expected conversion uplift or monetization plan — are you tracking revenue uplift per MAU or retention lift estimates?

What we’ll deliver next (internal + to you):
- Internal: a short unit-econ memo (1–2 pages) with 3 scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive) including: tokens/month, Redwood inference cost estimation, per-feature cost, and CAC payback given your stated conversion assumptions. (Marissa & Ben will own the math.)
- To CareLogix: an annotated pricing bucket that maps pilot usage to cost and recommended guardrails (burst caps, caching, quantization suggestions).

Quick note on timing: if you can send the DAU/avg tokens numbers by Fri, we’ll have the memo before your procurement review next Wed.

Cheers,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Recap + asks: Recommendation widget economics and next steps

Thanks Alex — quick answers inline below and attaching a small sample export of query-level logs.

DAU / usage (pilot 50k MAU target):
- DAU expected: 12k (initial pilot, i.e., ~24% of MAU)
- Avg queries/day per active user: 2.2
- Avg tokens per roundtrip (prompt + completion): ~260 tokens (we measured with current prototype)

Budget signal: procurement isn’t giving a hard cap yet, but stakeholder guidance is "pilot inference + tooling ideally < $120k/year" (this is the number I gave during the call).

Monetization / uplift assumptions:
- Primary KPI: 3% uplift in appointment bookings from exposed cohort vs control (we expect conservative 1.5% to 4% range).
- Revenue per incremental appointment (net): ~$80 (after payer reconciliation).

Attached: current-query-sample.csv (sanitized)

Let us know if you want a third column in the sample that tags by query type (clinical vs administrative).

—Marc
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marc Geller <marc.geller@carelogix.com>, Sara Lim <sara@carelogix.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Unit-econ memo: 3 scenarios and recommended pricing guardrails

Alex / Ben — I put together a short scenario set using the numbers Marc provided. Below are the core calculations and the recommended financing/ops guardrails we should share with CareLogix.

Assumptions (pilot):
- Pilot DAU: 12,000
- Avg queries/day: 2.2
- Avg tokens/query (roundtrip): 260
- Days/month: 30
- Pilot duration used for annualized estimate: 12 months (but we’ll show monthly numbers)

Raw tokens/month = DAU * queries/day * tokens/query * days = 12,000 * 2.2 * 260 * 30 = 2,059,200,000 tokens (~2059M)

Redwood estimated inference cost (per 1M tokens): we modeled three price points to reflect different model/quantization choices and routing policies:
- Conservative (high-quality model, less quantization): $85 / 1M tokens
- Expected (balanced perf & quant): $40 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive (quantized + batching + caching): $18 / 1M tokens

Monthly inference cost by scenario:
- Conservative: 2059 * $85 = $175,015 / month (~$2.1M / year)
- Expected: 2059 * $40 = $82,360 / month (~$988k / year)
- Aggressive: 2059 * $18 = $37,062 / month (~$444k / year)

Per-feature unit cost (per MAU-month): take monthly inference cost / MAU (50k target MAU, pilot DAU 12k but cost attributable to 50k since feature enabled for cohort):
- Conservative: $175,015 / 50,000 = $3.50 per MAU-month
- Expected: $82,360 / 50,000 = $1.65 per MAU-month
- Aggressive: $37,062 / 50,000 = $0.74 per MAU-month

Payback math (using Marc’s uplift numbers):
- Conservative scenario: assume 3% uplift on exposed cohort (multiply by DAU to get incremental appointments): incremental appointments/month = 12,000 * 3% = 360 appointments. Revenue net per appointment = $80 => incremental revenue = 360 * $80 = $28,800 / month.
  - Payback on inference cost only: $175,015 / 28,800 ≈ 6.1 months (not including CAC / other costs).
- Expected scenario: incremental revenue = $28,800 (same uplift) but cost = $82,360 => payback ≈ 2.86 months.
- Aggressive scenario: cost = $37,062 => payback ≈ 1.29 months.

If we convert payback into CAC payback: assume a launch marketing spend of $120k to acquire the initial exposed cohort (50k). Incremental revenue/month at expected scenario = $28,800 => CAC payback months = 120k / 28,800 ≈ 4.17 months. Under aggressive cost profile payback ≈ 1.52 months.

Margin targets (recommendation):
- CareLogix target gross margin on the feature line should be >= 60% after inference cost (i.e., inference should be <= 40% of incremental gross margin generated by the feature). Given per-appointment net revenue and expected uplift, the Expected scenario produces ~60–65% gross margin window if redemption and billing hold. Conservative scenario drives negative margin pressure unless model precision is significantly better than expected.

Operational guardrails we recommend to hit the Expected / Aggressive numbers:
- Use medium-sized model variant for inference with quantization options enabled (moves us from $85→$40 / 1M).
- Implement prefix caching for common queries (estimated to shave ~15% of tokens in practice).
- Set burst caps for the pilot and throttling to keep monthly spend predictable; enable alerting at 50% and 80% of forecasted spend.
- Start pilot with A/B testing so uplift estimates converge quickly; payback is highly sensitive to measured uplift (~±1% uplift changes payback materially).

Deliverables:
- Short memo (this email) + spreadsheet with line-item math (I attached to HubDrive link).
- Proposed contract clause: tiered per-1M pricing with option to re-evaluate after pilot. Suggested tiers: $40 /1M (baseline) with quantization add-on to get to $18 /1M for committed volumes or favorable model swap.

Questions for Alex / Ben before we send to Marc/Sara:
1) Are we comfortable proposing $40 /1M baseline for pilot (with clear note that actual model selection could change effective price)?
2) Should we include a short free-burst credit (e.g., first 100M tokens free) to reduce procurement friction?
3) Any other commercial levers you want to offer (SLA credits, onboarding hours)?

—Marissa
Director, Costing & Evals | Redwood Inference

This is excellent — thanks for the fast turnaround and clear scenarios. A couple quick items:

- Procurement will likely accept a baseline of $40 /1M if we can show the pilot keeps spend under $120k/year with the recommended guardrails.
- We definitely want the free-burst credit for the first 100M tokens to reduce the procurement ask — that would help close internal approvals.
- Please include a 30-day post-launch evaluation clause in the contract so we can re-open pricing if uplift falls under 1.5%.

Next step: can you and Ben join our procurement sync Friday 09:30AM PT? I’ll invite Marc and our procurement lead (I’ll include details in the calendar invite).

Thanks — Sara
